shifts.summary: The paper was overall moderate to difficult. Candidates reported good attempts ranging from 68 to 80 questions. Reasoning was generally easy to moderate, while GA was mostly moderate. Quant and English showed mixed difficulty levels. Time pressure was noted due to new sectional timing and scrolling issues.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported easy questions and fine timing.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS a bit easy overall; questions spread across history, geography, current affairs.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Time‑consuming; need to scroll right side; candidates could attempt only about 20 questions.

asked.q: Identify noun clauses in paragraph‑based questions
Lengthy arithmetic problems requiring extra time
Puzzle and matrix type questions appeared
Lengthier arithmetic and calculative problems were present
Vocabulary fill‑in‑the‑blank and RC passage were asked
Current affairs and static GK questions were asked
English moderate for repeaters, hard for beginners

observations: Sectional timing was introduced for the first time, increasing pressure.
Scrolling to the right side of the screen caused extra time loss.
Quant and GA were reported as the tougher sections.
Reasoning had the highest good‑attempt range.
disagreements: Reasoning difficulty split between Easy to Moderate and Moderate.
Quant difficulty split between Moderate to Difficult and Hard.
English difficulty varied, with some reports calling it Easy to Moderate and one noting it hard for beginners.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 28 October 2026 had three shifts. Shift 1 was reported as moderate to difficult overall, with candidates indicating good attempts ranging from 68 to 80 questions; these figures are unofficial and should be treated as approximate. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending, and no usable analysis has been published for them yet. SSC normalises scores across shifts to maintain fairness in the final ranking.
